per_case_results.query: How is the value of interest-free or concessional loan provided by employer for education/medical purposes calculated for a salaried employee under Rule 15 (2026 rules)?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 15 of the Income-tax Rules, 2026 (Table 5 - Valuation of Perquisites, sub-rule (1)), the value of an interest-free or concessional loan provided by an employer for education or medical purposes is calculated as the sum equal to the interest computed at the annual rate charged by the State Bank of India (as on the 1st day of the relevant tax year) for the maximum outstanding monthly balance, reduced by any interest already paid by the employee or their household member. For medical treatment loans (for diseases specified in Rule 18), no value is charged if the loan amount does not exceed Rs. 2,00,000 in the aggregate.

The rule has no effective date restriction (Effective Date: None), meaning it is fully applicable to all relevant tax years under the 2026 regime. The calculation is based on the tax year (AY) rather than the financial year (FY), with the rate determined as of the 1st day of the relevant tax year.

per_case_results.query: I am a senior citizen aged 77 who receives only pension and interest income. Can I submit a declaration to my bank under Rule 26D so that no tax return is required to be filed?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Yes, a 77-year-old senior citizen who receives only pension and interest income can submit a declaration under Rule 26D of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 to have tax deducted at source via their bank. However, this does NOT eliminate the mandatory requirement to file a regular income tax return (Form 16A/ITR-1). Rule 26D is a supplementary mechanism to ensure tax is deducted at source, while the standard return filing obligation remains unchanged.
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: Rule 26D was introduced with an effective date of 2-9-2021. Therefore, it applies to Assessment Years (AY) starting from AY 2021-22 onwards. For any AY before September 2, 2021, this rule was not in force and cannot be used.

per_case_results.query: I changed jobs during the previous year. What form must I submit to my current employer to declare salary and TDS from my previous employer under Rule 26A?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under Rule 26A of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, you must submit either Form No. 16 or Form No. 12BA to your current employer (the person responsible for making the salary payment) to declare your salary and TDS from your previous employer. Specifically, if your total salary from the previous employer was ₹1,50,000 or less, you must file Form No. 16. If it exceeded ₹1,50,000, you must file Form No. 12BA along with your income tax return.

per_case_results.query: As a central government employee, how is the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation determined?
per_case_results.direct_answer: Under the Income-tax Rules, 1962, the perquisite value of government-provided residential accommodation is determined using Table I (Valuation of Perquisites). For accommodation provided by the Central Government (or State Government) where the employer furnishes the accommodation, the value is calculated as the license fee determined by the Central Government plus 10% per annum of the cost of furniture (including television sets, radio sets, refrigerators, household appliances, air-conditioning plant or equipment). If the furniture is hired from a third party, the actual hire charges payable are used instead. This base value is then reduced by the rent actually paid by the employee. For unfurnished accommodation, the value is fixed at 24% of salary (with variations based on city population size as per the 2011 census).
per_case_results.temporal_applicability: This applies to the Financial Year (FY) 2021-22 and subsequent years assessed under the Assessment Year (AY) 2022-23 onwards. The effective date of these provisions is 1-9-2023 (as per Statutory Context 1, 2, 3, and 4). These are 1962 rules applied to modern fiscal years.
